translation.sourceText: Koine Greek New Testament — earliest substantial manuscript witnesses (Codex Vaticanus B/03 + Codex Sinaiticus א/01, 4th c. CE); SBLGNT base text; cross-collated against P45 (Chester Beatty I, ~250 CE) and the Western text of Codex Bezae (D/05, 5th c.) for Acts-specific variants. Acts 15:34 omitted in the Alexandrian critical text (absent in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus); preserved here as an empty verse-hole per critical convention, with the Western/Bezae interpolation documented in source apparatus.

paragraphs.text: Καί τινες κατελθόντες ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας ἐδίδασκον τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ὅτι Ἐὰν μὴ περιτμηθῆτε τῷ ἔθει τῷ Μωϋσέως, οὐ δύνασθε σωθῆναι.
paragraphs.translit: Kai tines katelthontes apo tēs Ioudaias edidaskon tous adelphous hoti Ean mē peritmēthēte tō ethei tō Mōuseōs, ou dynasthe sōthēnai.

i18n.en: And certain men came down from Judea and were teaching the brothers: "Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved."

paragraphs.text: γενομένης δὲ στάσεως καὶ ζητήσεως οὐκ ὀλίγης τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Βαρναβᾷ πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἔταξαν ἀναβαίνειν Παῦλον καὶ Βαρναβᾶν καί τινας ἄλλους ἐξ αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους καὶ πρεσβυτέρους εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ περὶ τοῦ ζητήματος τούτου.
paragraphs.translit: genomenēs de staseōs kai zētēseōs ouk oligēs tō Paulō kai tō Barnaba pros autous etaxan anabainein Paulon kai Barnaban kai tinas allous ex autōn pros tous apostolous kai presbyterous eis Ierousalēm peri tou zētēmatos toutou.

i18n.en: And when Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and debate with them, they appointed Paul and Barnabas and some others of them to go up to the apostles and elders in Jerusalem about this question.

paragraphs.text: οἱ μὲν οὖν προπεμφθέντες ὑπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας διήρχοντο τήν τε Φοινίκην καὶ Σαμάρειαν ἐκδιηγούμενοι τὴν ἐπιστροφὴν τῶν ἐθνῶν, καὶ ἐποίουν χαρὰν μεγάλην πᾶσι τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: hoi men oun propemphthentes hypo tēs ekklēsias diērchonto tēn te Phoinikēn kai Samareian ekdiēgoumenoi tēn epistrophēn tōn ethnōn, kai epoioun charan megalēn pasi tois adelphois.

i18n.en: Sent on their way by the church, they passed through both Phoenicia and Samaria, describing in detail the conversion of the Gentiles, and brought great joy to all the brothers.

paragraphs.text: παραγενόμενοι δὲ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ παρεδέχθησαν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας καὶ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων, ἀνήγγειλάν τε ὅσα ὁ θεὸς ἐποίησεν μετ’ αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: paragenomenoi de eis Ierousalēm paredechthēsan apo tēs ekklēsias kai tōn apostolōn kai tōn presbyterōn, anēngeilan te hosa ho theos epoiēsen met’ autōn.

i18n.en: And when they arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and the apostles and the elders, and they reported all that God had done with them.

paragraphs.text: ἐξανέστησαν δέ τινες τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς αἱρέσεως τῶν Φαρισαίων πεπιστευκότες, λέγοντες ὅτι δεῖ περιτέμνειν αὐτοὺς παραγγέλλειν τε τηρεῖν τὸν νόμον Μωϋσέως.
paragraphs.translit: exanestēsan de tines tōn apo tēs haireseōs tōn Pharisaiōn pepisteukotes, legontes hoti dei peritemnein autous parangellein te tērein ton nomon Mōuseōs.

i18n.en: But some of the sect of the Pharisees who had believed rose up, saying that it was necessary to circumcise them and to charge them to keep the law of Moses.

paragraphs.text: Συνήχθησάν τε οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἰδεῖν περὶ τοῦ λόγου τούτου.
paragraphs.translit: Synēchthēsan te hoi apostoloi kai hoi presbyteroi idein peri tou logou toutou.

i18n.en: And the apostles and the elders were gathered together to consider this matter.

paragraphs.text: πολλῆς δὲ ζητήσεως γενομένης ἀναστὰς Πέτρος εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε ὅτι ἀφ’ ἡμερῶν ἀρχαίων ἐν ὑμῖν ἐξελέξατο ὁ θεὸς διὰ τοῦ στόματός μου ἀκοῦσαι τὰ ἔθνη τὸν λόγον τοῦ εὐαγγελίου καὶ πιστεῦσαι·
paragraphs.translit: pollēs de zētēseōs genomenēs anastas Petros eipen pros autous· Andres adelphoi, hymeis epistasthe hoti aph’ hēmerōn archaiōn en hymin exelexato ho theos dia tou stomatos mou akousai ta ethnē ton logon tou euangeliou kai pisteusai·

i18n.en: And after there had been much debate, Peter stood up and said to them: "Brothers, you know that in the early days God made a choice among you, that by my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the gospel and believe.

notes.official: Peter's speech (vv.7-11) puts Pauline-sounding soteriology (justification-by-faith without works-of-the-law) on Peter's lips — a Lukan harmonization of the early-Christian leadership.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὁ καρδιογνώστης θεὸς ἐμαρτύρησεν αὐτοῖς δοὺς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον καθὼς καὶ ἡμῖν,
paragraphs.translit: kai ho kardiognōstēs theos emartyrēsen autois dous to pneuma to hagion kathōs kai hēmin,

i18n.en: And God, who knows the heart, bore witness to them by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as he did to us,

paragraphs.text: καὶ οὐθὲν διέκρινεν μεταξὺ ἡμῶν τε καὶ αὐτῶν, τῇ πίστει καθαρίσας τὰς καρδίας αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai outhen diekrinen metaxy hēmōn te kai autōn, tē pistei katharisas tas kardias autōn.

i18n.en: and he made no distinction between us and them, having cleansed their hearts by faith.

paragraphs.text: νῦν οὖν τί πειράζετε τὸν θεόν, ἐπιθεῖναι ζυγὸν ἐπὶ τὸν τράχηλον τῶν μαθητῶν ὃν οὔτε οἱ πατέρες ἡμῶν οὔτε ἡμεῖς ἰσχύσαμεν βαστάσαι;
paragraphs.translit: nyn oun ti peirazete ton theon, epitheinai zygon epi ton trachēlon tōn mathētōn hon oute hoi pateres hēmōn oute hēmeis ischysamen bastasai?

i18n.en: Now therefore, why are you testing God by placing on the neck of the disciples a yoke that neither our fathers nor we have been able to bear?

paragraphs.text: ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς χάριτος τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ πιστεύομεν σωθῆναι καθ’ ὃν τρόπον κἀκεῖνοι.
paragraphs.translit: alla dia tēs charitos tou kyriou Iēsou pisteuomen sōthēnai kath’ hon tropon kakeinoi.

i18n.en: But we believe that we shall be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, just as they will."

paragraphs.text: Ἐσίγησεν δὲ πᾶν τὸ πλῆθος, καὶ ἤκουον Βαρναβᾶ καὶ Παύλου ἐξηγουμένων ὅσα ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν δι’ αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: Esigēsen de pan to plēthos, kai ēkouon Barnaba kai Paulou exēgoumenōn hosa epoiēsen ho theos sēmeia kai terata en tois ethnesin di’ autōn.

i18n.en: And all the assembly fell silent, and they listened to Barnabas and Paul as they described what signs and wonders God had done through them among the Gentiles.

paragraphs.text: Μετὰ δὲ τὸ σιγῆσαι αὐτοὺς ἀπεκρίθη Ἰάκωβος λέγων· Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἀκούσατέ μου.
paragraphs.translit: Meta de to sigēsai autous apekrithē Iakōbos legōn· Andres adelphoi, akousate mou.

i18n.en: And after they had finished speaking, James answered, saying: "Brothers, listen to me.

paragraphs.text: Συμεὼν ἐξηγήσατο καθὼς πρῶτον ὁ θεὸς ἐπεσκέψατο λαβεῖν ἐξ ἐθνῶν λαὸν τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Symeōn exēgēsato kathōs prōton ho theos epeskepsato labein ex ethnōn laon tō onomati autou.

i18n.en: Simeon has described how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people for his name.

paragraphs.text: καὶ τούτῳ συμφωνοῦσιν οἱ λόγοι τῶν προφητῶν, καθὼς γέγραπται·
paragraphs.translit: kai toutō symphōnousin hoi logoi tōn prophētōn, kathōs gegraptai·

i18n.en: And with this the words of the prophets agree, as it is written:

paragraphs.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀναστρέψω καὶ ἀνοικοδομήσω τὴν σκηνὴν Δαυὶδ τὴν πεπτωκυῖαν, καὶ τὰ κατεσκαμμένα αὐτῆς ἀνοικοδομήσω καὶ ἀνορθώσω αὐτήν,
paragraphs.translit: Meta tauta anastrepsō kai anoikodomēsō tēn skēnēn Dauid tēn peptōkuian, kai ta kateskammena autēs anoikodomēsō kai anorthōsō autēn,

i18n.en: "After these things I will return and rebuild the fallen tent of David, and I will rebuild its ruins and set it up again,

paragraphs.text: ὅπως ἂν ἐκζητήσωσιν οἱ κατάλοιποι τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὸν κύριον, καὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐφ’ οὓς ἐπικέκληται τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐπ’ αὐτούς, λέγει κύριος ποιῶν ταῦτα
paragraphs.translit: hopōs an ekzētēsōsin hoi kataloipoi tōn anthrōpōn ton kyrion, kai panta ta ethnē eph’ hous epikeklētai to onoma mou ep’ autous, legei kyrios poiōn tauta

i18n.en: that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, even all the Gentiles upon whom my name has been called — says the Lord, who does these things

paragraphs.text: γνωστὰ ἀπ’ αἰῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: gnōsta ap’ aiōnos.

i18n.en: known from of old."

paragraphs.text: διὸ ἐγὼ κρίνω μὴ παρενοχλεῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐπιστρέφουσιν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν,
paragraphs.translit: dio egō krinō mē parenochlein tois apo tōn ethnōn epistrephousin epi ton theon,

i18n.en: Therefore my judgment is that we should not trouble those of the Gentiles who are turning to God,

notes.official: **MAJOR APOSTOLIC-DECREE SITE.** James' proposal (Acts 15:19-21) and the resulting decree-letter (15:23-29) establish the four-fold prohibition for Gentile-Christian membership: (i) idol-sacrifices; (ii) blood; (iii) strangled-things; (iv) porneia. Cross-corpus to Lev 17-18 (ger toshav / resident-alien commandments) and the rabbinic Noahide-commandments tradition. Documented at central-glossary entry `apostolic-decree-acts-15-noahide-leviticus-17-18-cross-corpus`. The Bauckham 1995 + Witherington 1998 + Bockmuehl 2000 monographs document the Lev 17-18 ger toshav background hypothesis.

paragraphs.text: ἀλλὰ ἐπιστεῖλαι αὐτοῖς τοῦ ἀπέχεσθαι τῶν ἀλισγημάτων τῶν εἰδώλων καὶ τῆς πορνείας καὶ τοῦ πνικτοῦ καὶ τοῦ αἵματος·
paragraphs.translit: alla episteilai autois tou apechesthai tōn alisgēmatōn tōn eidōlōn kai tēs porneias kai tou pniktou kai tou haimatos·

i18n.en: but should write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, and from sexual immorality, and from what is strangled, and from blood.

notes.official: The four prohibitions: *alisgēmatōn tōn eidōlōn / porneias / pniktou / haimatos* — pollutions-of-idols + porneia + strangled-things + blood. The v.20 ordering (idol-pollutions + porneia + strangled-things + blood) differs from the v.29 ordering (idol-sacrifices + blood + strangled-things + porneia) — both preserved in the modern critical text. The four prohibitions are drawn from Lev 17-18 ger toshav commandments addressed to non-Israelite-residents.

paragraphs.text: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ ἐκ γενεῶν ἀρχαίων κατὰ πόλιν τοὺς κηρύσσοντας αὐτὸν ἔχει ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον ἀναγινωσκόμενος.
paragraphs.translit: Mōusēs gar ek geneōn archaiōn kata polin tous kēryssontas auton echei en tais synagōgais kata pan sabbaton anaginōskomenos.

i18n.en: For from generations of old Moses has had those who proclaim him in every city, being read in the synagogues every Sabbath."

notes.official: James' final rationale: *Mōusēs gar ek geneōn archaiōn kata polin tous kēryssontas auton echei en tais synagōgais kata pan sabbaton anaginōskomenos* 'For Moses from ancient generations has in every city those who preach him, being read in the synagogues every sabbath'. Two main interpretive lines: (i) the Sabbath-synagogue rationale (the prohibitions are chosen because they are familiar from the synagogue-Sabbath-Torah-reading); (ii) the Jewish-Christian-community rationale (the prohibitions enable table-fellowship between Jewish-Christians and Gentile-Christians in mixed congregations). Both readings have textual warrant.

paragraphs.text: Τότε ἔδοξε τοῖς ἀποστόλοις καὶ τοῖς πρεσβυτέροις σὺν ὅλῃ τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἐκλεξαμένους ἄνδρας ἐξ αὐτῶν πέμψαι εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν σὺν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ Βαρναβᾷ, Ἰούδαν τὸν καλούμενον Βαρσαββᾶν καὶ Σιλᾶν, ἄνδρας ἡγουμένους ἐν τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς,
paragraphs.translit: Tote edoxe tois apostolois kai tois presbyterois syn holē tē ekklēsia eklexamenous andras ex autōn pempsai eis Antiocheian syn tō Paulō kai Barnaba, Ioudan ton kaloumenon Barsabban kai Silan, andras hēgoumenous en tois adelphois,

i18n.en: Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, with the whole church, to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas — Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, leading men among the brothers,

paragraphs.text: γράψαντες διὰ χειρὸς αὐτῶν· Οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἀδελφοὶ τοῖς κατὰ τὴν Ἀντιόχειαν καὶ Συρίαν καὶ Κιλικίαν ἀδελφοῖς τοῖς ἐξ ἐθνῶν χαίρειν.
paragraphs.translit: grapsantes dia cheiros autōn· Hoi apostoloi kai hoi presbyteroi adelphoi tois kata tēn Antiocheian kai Syrian kai Kilikian adelphois tois ex ethnōn chairein.

i18n.en: with this letter delivered by their hand: "The apostles and the elders, brothers, to the brothers from the Gentiles in Antioch and Syria and Cilicia: greetings.

paragraphs.text: Ἐπειδὴ ἠκούσαμεν ὅτι τινὲς ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐτάραξαν ὑμᾶς λόγοις ἀνασκευάζοντες τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν, οἷς οὐ διεστειλάμεθα,
paragraphs.translit: Epeidē ēkousamen hoti tines ex hēmōn etaraxan hymas logois anaskeuazontes tas psychas hymōn, hois ou diesteilametha,

i18n.en: Since we have heard that some who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your souls — though we gave them no instructions —

paragraphs.text: ἔδοξεν ἡμῖν γενομένοις ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐκλεξαμένοις ἄνδρας πέμψαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς σὺν τοῖς ἀγαπητοῖς ἡμῶν Βαρναβᾷ καὶ Παύλῳ,
paragraphs.translit: edoxen hēmin genomenois homothymadon eklexamenois andras pempsai pros hymas syn tois agapētois hēmōn Barnaba kai Paulō,

i18n.en: it seemed good to us, having come to one accord, to choose men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,

paragraphs.text: ἀνθρώποις παραδεδωκόσι τὰς ψυχὰς αὐτῶν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: anthrōpois paradedōkosi tas psychas autōn hyper tou onomatos tou kyriou hēmōn Iēsou Christou.

i18n.en: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.

paragraphs.text: ἀπεστάλκαμεν οὖν Ἰούδαν καὶ Σιλᾶν, καὶ αὐτοὺς διὰ λόγου ἀπαγγέλλοντας τὰ αὐτά.
paragraphs.translit: apestalkamen oun Ioudan kai Silan, kai autous dia logou apangellontas ta auta.

i18n.en: We have therefore sent Judas and Silas, who will themselves tell you the same things by word of mouth.

paragraphs.text: ἔδοξεν γὰρ τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ καὶ ἡμῖν μηδὲν πλέον ἐπιτίθεσθαι ὑμῖν βάρος πλὴν τούτων τῶν ἐπάναγκες,
paragraphs.translit: edoxen gar tō pneumati tō hagiō kai hēmin mēden pleon epitithesthai hymin baros plēn toutōn tōn epanankes,

i18n.en: For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things:

paragraphs.text: ἀπέχεσθαι εἰδωλοθύτων καὶ αἵματος καὶ πνικτῶν καὶ πορνείας· ἐξ ὧν διατηροῦντες ἑαυτοὺς εὖ πράξετε. ἔρρωσθε.
paragraphs.translit: apechesthai eidōlothytōn kai haimatos kai pniktōn kai porneias· ex hōn diatērountes heautous eu praxete. Errōsthe.

i18n.en: that you abstain from things sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from what is strangled, and from sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell."

notes.official: The decree-letter v.29 ordering: idol-sacrifices + blood + strangled-things + porneia. **MAJOR TEXTUAL-CRITICAL LAYER.** The Western text (Codex Bezae D/05) deploys a different reading: three-fold prohibition (idol-pollutions + blood + porneia) omitting 'strangled-things' AND adding the negative-Golden-Rule (*kai hosa mē thelete heautois ginesthai heterō mē poiein* 'and whatever you do not want done to yourselves, do not do to others'). The Western reading is widely interpreted as a 2nd-c. redaction emphasizing the moral over the dietary requirements after the Gentile-Christian-community had become demographically-dominant. The WoH-Translation preserves the Alexandrian critical-text four-fold prohibition per NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT.

paragraphs.text: Οἱ μὲν οὖν ἀπολυθέντες κατῆλθον εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, καὶ συναγαγόντες τὸ πλῆθος ἐπέδωκαν τὴν ἐπιστολήν·
paragraphs.translit: Hoi men oun apolythentes katēlthon eis Antiocheian, kai synagagontes to plēthos epedōkan tēn epistolēn·

i18n.en: So they, having been sent off, went down to Antioch, and gathering the assembly together, delivered the letter.

paragraphs.text: ἀναγνόντες δὲ ἐχάρησαν ἐπὶ τῇ παρακλήσει.
paragraphs.translit: anagnontes de echarēsan epi tē paraklēsei.

i18n.en: And when they had read it, they rejoiced at the encouragement.

paragraphs.text: Ἰούδας τε καὶ Σιλᾶς, καὶ αὐτοὶ προφῆται ὄντες, διὰ λόγου πολλοῦ παρεκάλεσαν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἐπεστήριξαν·
paragraphs.translit: Ioudas te kai Silas, kai autoi prophētai ontes, dia logou pollou parekalesan tous adelphous kai epestērixan·

i18n.en: And Judas and Silas, themselves being prophets, encouraged the brothers with many words and strengthened them.

paragraphs.text: ποιήσαντες δὲ χρόνον ἀπελύθησαν μετ’ εἰρήνης ἀπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστείλαντας αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: poiēsantes de chronon apelythēsan met’ eirēnēs apo tōn adelphōn pros tous aposteilantas autous.

i18n.en: And after spending some time, they were sent off in peace by the brothers to those who had sent them.

notes.official: **TEXTUAL HOLE.** v.34 is ABSENT in Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + Alexandrinus + P74 + the modern critical text. The verse is present in Bezae (D) and some Byzantine witnesses with the text *edoxe de tō Sila epimeinai autou* 'but it seemed good to Silas to remain there' — a Western interpolation smoothing the apparent narrative-inconsistency (v.33 says Judas and Silas were sent back to Antioch; v.40 has Paul taking Silas). The WoH-Translation preserves the modern critical-text convention: verse-number 34 is preserved as a 'hole'. See overlay-glossary entry `acts-15-34-empty-verse-hole-western-interpolation-convention`.

paragraphs.text: Παῦλος δὲ καὶ Βαρναβᾶς διέτριβον ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ διδάσκοντες καὶ εὐαγγελιζόμενοι μετὰ καὶ ἑτέρων πολλῶν τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου.
paragraphs.translit: Paulos de kai Barnabas dietribon en Antiocheia didaskontes kai euangelizomenoi meta kai heterōn pollōn ton logon tou kyriou.

i18n.en: But Paul and Barnabas remained in Antioch, teaching and proclaiming the good news of the word of the Lord, with many others also.

paragraphs.text: Μετὰ δέ τινας ἡμέρας εἶπεν πρὸς Βαρναβᾶν Παῦλος· Ἐπιστρέψαντες δὴ ἐπισκεψώμεθα τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς κατὰ πᾶσαν πόλιν ἐν αἷς κατηγγείλαμεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου, πῶς ἔχουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: Meta de tinas hēmeras eipen pros Barnaban Paulos· Epistrepsantes dē episkepsōmetha tous adelphous kata pasan polin en hais katēngeilamen ton logon tou kyriou, pōs echousin.

i18n.en: And after some days, Paul said to Barnabas: "Let us return and visit the brothers in every city where we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing."

notes.official: The Paul-Barnabas split (vv.36-41): the *paroxysmos* (sharp disagreement) over John Mark's earlier desertion at Pamphylia (Acts 13:13) leads to the two-mission-team split. The Lukan-Acts narrative does not resolve the rights-and-wrongs of the split; the narrative function is to establish the two-fold mission pattern (Paul + Silas to Syria-Cilicia + Asia Minor; Barnabas + John Mark to Cyprus).

paragraphs.text: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ ἐβούλετο συμπαραλαβεῖν καὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην τὸν καλούμενον Μᾶρκον·
paragraphs.translit: Barnabas de ebouleto symparalabein kai ton Iōannēn ton kaloumenon Markon·

i18n.en: And Barnabas wanted to take along John, who was called Mark.

paragraphs.text: Παῦλος δὲ ἠξίου, τὸν ἀποστάντα ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Παμφυλίας καὶ μὴ συνελθόντα αὐτοῖς εἰς τὸ ἔργον, μὴ συμπαραλαμβάνειν τοῦτον.
paragraphs.translit: Paulos de ēxiou, ton apostanta ap’ autōn apo Pamphylias kai mē synelthonta autois eis to ergon, mē symparalambanein touton.

i18n.en: But Paul thought it best not to take along the one who had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work.

paragraphs.text: ἐγένετο δὲ παροξυσμὸς ὥστε ἀποχωρισθῆναι αὐτοὺς ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων, τόν τε Βαρναβᾶν παραλαβόντα τὸν Μᾶρκον ἐκπλεῦσαι εἰς Κύπρον.
paragraphs.translit: egeneto de paroxysmos hōste apochōristhēnai autous ap’ allēlōn, ton te Barnaban paralabonta ton Markon ekpleusai eis Kypron.

i18n.en: And there arose a sharp disagreement, so that they separated from one another, and Barnabas took Mark and sailed away to Cyprus.

paragraphs.text: Παῦλος δὲ ἐπιλεξάμενος Σιλᾶν ἐξῆλθεν παραδοθεὶς τῇ χάριτι τοῦ κυρίου ὑπὸ τῶν ἀδελφῶν,
paragraphs.translit: Paulos de epilexamenos Silan exēlthen paradotheis tē chariti tou kyriou hypo tōn adelphōn,

i18n.en: But Paul chose Silas and departed, having been commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: διήρχετο δὲ τὴν Συρίαν καὶ Κιλικίαν ἐπιστηρίζων τὰς ἐκκλησίας.
paragraphs.translit: diērcheto de tēn Syrian kai Kilikian epistērizōn tas ekklēsias.

i18n.en: And he went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
